scheme1_name: CBSE Merit Scholarship Scheme for Single Girl Child (SGC)
disclaimer: This is AI-generated guidance based on official records. It is NOT an official notification. Please verify with official sources before applying. For legal or financial decisions, consult the respective ministry's official website or contact them directly.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Financial assistance to meritorious single girl students in classes 11-12 to promote girls' education and recognise small families.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Crop insurance to protect farmers financially against crop losses from natural disasters, pests, and diseases.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Single girl child (only child; twins born together also count) in class 11-12, studying in CBSE school, with 70%+ in class 10, family income ≤ Rs. 8 lakh/year, Indian national.
comparisons.scheme2_value: All farmers (including tenant/sharecroppers) growing notified crops in notified areas, with valid land ownership/tenure agreement.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 1,000/month for max 2 years (classes 11-12 only); total max Rs. 24,000. Disbursed via bank (NEFT/ECS).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Affordable premium (farmer pays 1.5%-5%, govt subsidizes rest); covers crop loss, natural disasters, pests, diseases, post-harvest losses (14 days); claims within ~2 months.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Max Rs. 2,500/month in class 10; max Rs. 3,000/month in classes 11-12 (strict eligibility cap). NRI: up to Rs. 6,000/month.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Not applicable (scheme is for farmers, not students).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Family gross income ≤ Rs. 8 lakh/year (proven via attested affidavit on Rs. 50 stamp paper).
comparisons.scheme2_value: No income limit mentioned; eligibility depends on crop/area notification and land ownership.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Passport photo, signature (scanned), Aadhaar card, admission proof, student ID, class 10 mark sheet, Aadhaar-linked bank account details, school-verified fee receipt, income affidavit (attested by Gazetted Officer/SDM/First-Class Magistrate), signed undertaking.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Passport photo, bank passbook, identity proof (Aadhaar/PAN/Voter ID/NREGA card), address proof (Aadhaar/PAN/Voter ID/electricity bill), land records (RoR/LPC/agreement), crop declaration.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online at cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/scholar.html: register, enter class 10 roll & DOB, prepare undertaking & affidavit per guidelines, scan & upload PDFs (max 1 MB). School verification mandatory. Renewals: mail signed confirmation to CBSE.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Online at pmfby.gov.in: register as guest farmer, fill farmer/residential/account details, upload documents, submit, make payment. Offline via CSC also available. Track status on portal.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Yearly windows notified on CBSE scholarship page (check current session dates). No fixed all-India deadline provided.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Apply within ~2 weeks of sowing season start (state-specific cut-off dates notified on pmfby.gov.in). Missing deadline = no cover for that season.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Valid for max 2 years (classes 11-12); renewals require class 11 mark sheet and good conduct/regular attendance.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Must enrol each season; no automatic rollover. Requires timely application within sowing window each season.

comparisons.scheme1_value: ❌ Tuition fee above limits = ineligible. ❌ Family income > Rs. 8 lakh = ineligible. ❌ Non-single girl child ineligible. ❌ Regular attendance & good conduct mandatory. ❌ Not for non-CBSE schools.
comparisons.scheme2_value: ❌ Non-notified crops/areas not covered. ❌ Crop losses from negligence/non-compliance rejected. ❌ Must not receive compensation from other sources. ❌ Post-harvest cover = 14 days only. ❌ Non-payment = coverage cancelled.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Ministry of Education; implemented by CBSE (Central Board of Secondary Education).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare; implemented by insurance companies & banks.

key_differences_summary: SCHEME 1 (SGC) is for **single girls in school** (class 11-12), supports education with monthly cash; SCHEME 2 (PMFBY) is for **farmers**, protects crops with insurance. They serve completely different groups and goals — pick based on who you are: a student or a farmer.
recommendation: These schemes target entirely different beneficiaries. **If you are a single girl student in class 11-12 with good marks and low family income**, apply for SGC Scholarship via cbse.gov.in. **If you are a farmer growing crops**, apply for PMFBY crop insurance via pmfby.gov.in within your state's sowing season window.
